title: Heer and Ranjha
author: Waris Shah
paraphrase: Ranjha, a young man who leaves his village after a family quarrel, takes work tending buffalo in the household of Heer's father. He and Heer fall in love, but her family marries her to another man, and the lovers' story ends in loss.
landscape_link: The tale's world is one of cattle, river-fed pasture and seasonal farm work on the Punjab plains, the same kind of landscape this site watches from orbit. The poem is not set at this exact spot.
source: Waris Shah, Heer (1766), public domain; retold in the FASAL author's own words. CITATION_NEEDED: add the edition or translation you consulted.

title: Sassui and Punhun
author: Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai
paraphrase: Sassui, a girl raised in a washerman's family, falls in love with Punhun, a prince from Kech. His brothers carry him away while she sleeps, and she follows across hills and desert in a search that ends in tragedy.
landscape_link: Sassui's journey belongs to lower Sindh and the dry hills toward Balochistan, not specifically to Larkana. It is used here as Sindhi regional heritage beside the Indus plain.
source: Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai, Shah jo Risalo (18th century), public domain; retold in the FASAL author's own words. CITATION_NEEDED: add the edition or translation you consulted.

title: Umar and Marvi
author: Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai
paraphrase: Marvi, a village girl from the Thar desert, is taken to the fort of the ruler Umar. She refuses his wealth and keeps longing for her own people and wells, and in the end she is allowed to return home.
landscape_link: The story is rooted in Thar, a rain-fed desert where village life depends on water and the monsoon, which makes it a fitting companion for this site.
source: Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai, Shah jo Risalo (18th century), public domain; retold in the FASAL author's own words. CITATION_NEEDED: add the edition or translation you consulted.
